statement: This sketch simulates Conway's Game of Life in a constantly evolving grid of illuminated cells. The patterns of active cells change over time, creating an organic appearance of growth and decay. Each cell follows the classic rules: alive cells die if they have fewer than two or more than three neighbors, and dead cells become alive if they have exactly three neighbors. When a cell dies, it emits a bright flash before disappearing, providing visual feedback for the simulation's dynamics. The background subtly darkens with each generation cycle, enhancing the sense of perpetual motion. The system runs autonomously without any user input, continuously updating the canvas to display natural, evolving patterns.
